provenance.note: Curated waterlogging register (the Mumbai chronic-spots pattern): Delhi publishes no machine-readable hotspot list, so this carries the named perennial sites with landmark coordinates and keeps the full official lists (169 identified locations 2025; 448 traffic-police-mapped points) as a named gap. Per-entry press/reporting citations and summary.sources carry the accountability; location_basis per entry marks landmark, not survey, positions.

note: Delhi's chronic waterlogging register (the Mumbai chronic-spots pattern, Chennai-parity row for the 2015-hotspots layer). Delhi publishes no machine-readable hotspot list; what IS public is a hierarchy of counts plus a stable set of named perennial sites that appear in every year's monsoon-action reporting. This register carries the named perennials with landmark coordinates and keeps the full official lists as a named gap (PWD monsoon action plan document / RTI). Coordinates are landmark positions (metro station, underpass, flyover), not survey points - location_basis per entry.

hotspots.name: Minto Bridge underpass
hotspots.location_basis: Minto Road railway bridge underpass, Connaught Place edge
hotspots.why: Delhi's emblematic waterlogging site - the drowned-bus photograph of every monsoon; a 2020 drowning death made it the PWD's flagship fix (dedicated pump house + CCTV + alerts).
hotspots.status_2026: Reported flood-free through early monsoon 2026 after pumping upgrades

hotspots.name: Pul Prahladpur underpass
hotspots.location_basis: MB Road railway underpass, south-east Delhi
hotspots.why: Deepest of the chronic underpasses; a 2024 drowning kept it on the perennial list; sump + pump capacity repeatedly upgraded.

hotspots.name: Ring Road opposite WHO building (IP Estate)
hotspots.location_basis: Mahatma Gandhi Marg opposite the WHO/IP Estate frontage
hotspots.why: Low saucer on the Ring Road beside the Yamuna floodplain - doubles as a river-flood exposure point (2023 inundation reached this stretch).

hotspots.name: Jahangirpuri Metro Station Road
hotspots.location_basis: GT Karnal Road at Jahangirpuri Metro station
hotspots.why: North-west Delhi chronic point where trunk drainage meets the GT Road corridor.

hotspots.name: Zakhira flyover underpass
hotspots.location_basis: Zakhira crossing, Rohtak Road / railway lines
hotspots.why: West Delhi's rail-corridor sump; among the four underpasses PWD showcases when they stay dry.

hotspots.name: Loni Road Golchakkar
hotspots.why: East Delhi chronic point on the Shahdara drain catchment - trans-Yamuna's representative on the perennial list.

hotspots.name: Karala-Kanjhawala stretch
hotspots.why: Outer-Delhi flat terrain with no trunk drainage - the perennial list's reminder that waterlogging is not only a core-city problem.

hotspots.name: Dhaula Kuan underpass
hotspots.why: Historic chokepoint at the Ridge's runoff line; in PWD's four-underpass showcase set.

hotspots.name: Moolchand underpass
hotspots.location_basis: Ring Road at Moolchand (Lajpat Nagar edge)
hotspots.why: South Delhi's chronic underpass on the Barapullah catchment; in PWD's four-underpass showcase set.

gaps: The full official lists (169 identified locations 2025; 448 traffic-police-mapped points 2023-25; 71 nodal-officer sites) are referenced in reporting but not published as data - PWD monsoon action plan document ask / RTI target.
No outcome data per hotspot per event (which sites actually flooded, when) - the traffic police advisories during rain events are the reconstruction source for a future season log.
